title: P60 Etoile, Elysee, Monthlery and Monaco: what differences really matter
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: The P60 multiplies names and trim levels. To buy or restore the right car, one has to separate what belongs to presentation, equipment and commercial positioning.
content:
The P60 range impresses through abundance. That excess forms part of Simca’s charm, yet it also makes today’s cars harder to read when one wants to know exactly what stands before them.

Names meant to cover the whole market

Etoile, Elysee, Monthlery and Monaco each place the car at a different level of trim, image or market position. Simca uses this multiplication to reach a wider audience without building a wholly new car each time.

The method works commercially, but today it needs a little method to be read correctly.

Visible differences matter more than names alone

Chrome level, fabrics, instruments, upholstery details, body type and equipment all help separate a coherent version from a car rebuilt out of nearby parts.

On a P60, catalogue words do not suffice. One has to check that the whole presentation tells the same story.

Buy the right version rather than an attractive name

The classic risk lies in paying for a seductive label without checking whether the car truly matches its definition. A Monaco or Monthlery only matters if the overall coherence still holds.

That is why version reading remains essential. It protects both collecting quality and restoration budget.
